study_identification.title: Charting brain growth and aging at high spatial precision

study_characteristics.study_objective: To create lifespan brain charts of cortical thickness and subcortical volume derived from structural MRI, to serve as reference models for population variation and to study individual deviations.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABCD, ABIDE, ADHD200, CAMCAN, CMI-HBN, HCP-Aging, HCP-Development, HCP-Early Psychosis, HCP-Young Adult, IXI, NKI-RS, Oasis, OpenNeuro, PNC, SRPBS, and UKBiobank)

quality_checking_detail.answer: A subset of the full data set underwent manual quality checking (mQC) by an expert rater. For the full sample, a semi-automated QC was used. The ABCD study data distributes a variable (freesqc01.t1.mriqc_pred) that was used for QC.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Site variation was modeled using fixed effects in a warped Bayesian linear regression model.

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex are fixed effects. Site is modeled as a fixed effect.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper explicitly states that site variation was modeled using fixed effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Site variation was modeled using fixed effects, which we have shown in prior work provides relatively good performance

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation on non-independent data within the same domain.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper reports out-of-sample metrics on a held-out test set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: We split the available data into training and test sets, stratifying by site... we report out of sample metrics

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper demonstrates how to transfer the models to new samples (i.e., data not present in the initial training set) using a transfer dataset from OpenNeuro.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Finally, to facilitate independent validation, we packaged pretrained models and code for transferring to new samples into an open resource for use by the community and demonstrated how to transfer the models to new samples (i.e., data not present in the initial training set).

clinical_dataset.answer: ABIDE; ADHD200; CNP; SRPBS; Delta; HCP-EP; KCL; UMich_CWS; UMich_SAD; UMich_SZG; TOP

diseases_studied.answer: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); Early Psychosis (EP); Schizophrenia (SZ); Bipolar Disorder (BD); Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)

clinical_groups_sex.answer: ADHD: F36% M64%; ASD: F14% M86%; EP: F38% M62%; SZ: F41% M59%; BD: NR; MDD: F50% M50%

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Case-control comparisons on the raw cortical thickness and subcortical volumes, and on the deviation maps.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The created lifespan brain charts of cortical thickness and subcortical volume can be used to quantify variability underlying multiple psychiatric disorders whilst also refining case-control inferences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The models provide the opportunity for mapping the diverse trajectories of different brain areas, explaining up to 80% of the variance out of sample. The individual-level deviations provide complimentary information to the group effects, and for most diagnostic groups, the z-statistics derived from the normative deviations also provided stronger case-control effects than the raw data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The word 'normative' is problematic. The curated data set is based on aggregating existing data, meaning there is unavoidable sampling bias (e.g., WEIRD societies). Semi-automated quality control for the full sample. Freesurfer was not adjusted for the very young age ranges (2-7 yo).
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The models and code are made available to the research community, with an online interactive visualization tool and tutorial code notebooks.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper provides a comprehensive resource for normative modeling of brain imaging data, including pre-trained models, software tools, and detailed documentation. The authors encourage the use of the term 'reference cohort' over 'normative model'.
